topic: Full content inventory + IA audit of Dr. Satish Regonda's existing Google Sites site (sites.google.com/iith.ac.in/satishregonda), plus verified status of raftwaters.in and all outbound links/assets.
key_findings: The site has exactly 13 published pages, not the 11 in the nav. Two are ORPHANED (reachable only via inline body links, absent from the menu): /research/climate-extremes-societal-resiliency-krishna-river-basin and /research/climate-extremes-societal-resiliency-krishna-river-basin/fgd-workshop-krishna-river-basin. Guessed slugs news, awards, cv, contact, gallery, alumni, projects, positions, people, team, group, publications, courses, blog, media, outreach ALL return 404 — so there is no CV, no news, no awards, and no contact page today.

raftwaters.in DOES NOT EXIST IN DNS. Verified NXDOMAIN (Status:3) against both Google DoH (dns.google) and Cloudflare DoH for A and NS records; curl and WebFetch both fail with ENOTFOUND/getaddrinfo. It is not 'a separate site that exists' — there is nothing to link to yet. The project brief's premise is wrong.

satishregonda.in ALSO does not resolve — verified NXDOMAIN on both resolvers. The purchased domain has no nameservers/DNS delegation set up yet. Someone has to do that before any hosting decision matters.

raftwaters.com is registered but unrelated to the lab: it is a GoDaddy Website Builder placeholder titled 'Raft Waters' with the tagline 'Ride the Rapids with Us' and meta description 'Raftwaters.com is launching soon! Stay tuned for updates on our website development services.' Do not link to it.

snapflood.in IS registered (A records 3.33.251.168, 15.197.225.128) and 301-redirects to https://www.snapflood.civil.iith.ac.in/ — which is itself NXDOMAIN. So snapflood.in is a live-but-broken redirect chain today. This is a real, fixable asset the new site could point at.

The publication list is substantial and current: 29 refereed journal papers (through 2026), 2 book chapters, 23 conference presentations, 2 invited seminars, 1 scientific activity (AGU 2021 session H111 convener), 3 web products. Google Scholar (user=cTXdUlUAAAAJ) reports 1,859 citations, h-index 15, i10-index 20 (587 / 12 / 15 since 2021).

Three verified-broken publication links: (a) https://doi.org/10.1175/JHM-D-22-0160.1. returns 404 because of a trailing period (drop it and it 200s); (b) https://authors.elsevier.com/c/1ebIn7s~EVp4te returns HTTP 400 — an expired Elsevier 50-day share link used as the title link for Mohammed et al. 2022 Urban Climate; (c) Anupoju et al. 2021 lists DOI 10.1061/(ASCE).WR.1943-5452.0001406 which Crossref 404s — the correct DOI is 10.1061/(ASCE)WR.1943-5452.0001406 (stray period after the closing paren).

Brown et al. 2014 Part 1 and Part 2 are both printed with the SAME DOI (10.1016/j.jhydrol.2014.05.030). Crossref confirms they are two distinct records: Part 1 = 10.1016/j.jhydrol.2014.05.030, Part 2 = 10.1016/j.jhydrol.2014.05.028.

The RAFT page's SnapFlood Google Form link is a concatenated double URL — href="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSclN-.../viewformhttps://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSclN-.../viewform" — verified 404. The same page also reads 'SnapFlood Google from link a nd X' (typo 'from' for 'form', broken word 'a nd').

The RAFT page is badly stale relative to the Students page. It headlines Surya Kiran and Padmini as 'PhD Scholars' — both defended (Padmini viva Feb 2025, Surya Kiran viva Feb 2026). Its 'MTech Students' (Swagatam, Kanishka, Shruti) all graduated in 2025. It omits 7 people the Students page lists as current: H. S. Abdul Baasit M. P., Bharathi Radha Josyula, Gaurav Bapurao Khairnar, Subhadip Datta, Deepak, Rahul Thangallapally, Essapally Naresh.

A PhD student is missing entirely from the personal site: Akansha Maity (Dept. of Climate Change, PhD 2023 cohort), Guide: Dr. Satish Regonda, Co-Guide: Dr. Shruti Upadhyaya, research area 'Bias correction of rainfall forecasts using AI/ML' — verified on https://cc.iith.ac.in/students.html.

There is NO photograph of Dr. Regonda anywhere on his own site. The home page has zero content images — only the site logo in the header and a decorative banner. His only official portrait lives at https://iith.ac.in/assets/images/profiles/Satish.png.

Every image is hosted on lh3.googleusercontent.com/sitesv/... and returns HTTP 403 to any non-browser client, with or without a Referer header (tested). Images cannot be hotlinked or scripted-scraped for the migration — they must be pulled via Google Takeout or manually saved from a signed-in browser session. 22 distinct image URLs exist across the site (list in details).

The entire 'Guidelines for Sixer Twitter' page is one image (class CENy8b) with NO alt text and only ~20 words of surrounding text. The guidelines themselves are unreadable to search engines and screen readers. The page also duplicates its own heading and link twice.

The site runs Universal Analytics UA-138718262-1, which Google shut down in July 2023 — it has been collecting nothing for 3 years. There is no canonical tag, no per-page meta description, and every page shares og:title 'Satish R' (the site's display name, not his real name) with the site logo as og:image.

Contact details are inconsistent and deliberately obfuscated across pages: home says 'Kandi - 502285' / 'Tel : +91-40- 2301 6315 (O)' / 'satishr.at.iith.ac.in'; the urban-flood, opportunities and FGD pages say 'satishr.at.ce.iith.ac.in'; only the SnapFlood page uses real addresses (mailto:snapflood@iith.ac.in, satishr@ce.iith.ac.in); the official IITH page says 'Kandi-502284', 'Room: B-212', 'Office Phone: (040) 2359 - 6315', satishr@ce.iith.ac.in.

The RAFT acronym is expanded two different ways on the same site: 'Rainfall-runoff Analysis modelling and Forecasting Tools' (RAFT page, home) vs 'Rainfall-runoff Analysis and Forecasting Tools' (SnapFlood page and the Play Store listing). A canonical form has to be chosen.

There is a named mascot, 'VarshaMitra', introduced in the group's UFIS video — it appears nowhere on the website. Verified in the description of https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zz9i62ucZ3c ('Urban Flood Information System by Raft Group', IIT Hyderabad channel, uploaded 2023-10-04, 1,025 views).

Verified press coverage exists that the site never mentions: newsmeter.in ('IIT-H researchers to develop data-driven tech to alert Hyderabad on floods'), thehansindia.com ('IITH initiates a groundbreaking endeavor to tackle persistent issue of urban flooding in Hyderabad'), deccanchronicle.com ('Innovative Urban Flood Information System aims to transform city's resilience'). All three fetched HTTP 200.

All three R/Shiny products are alive — they return 202 on first hit (shinyapps.io cold start) then 200: ExtremeClimateAnalysis_Serayu_Krishna_RiverBasins, HydroEMOS, PvrtyAppV03. They are on a hibernating free-tier pattern, so first load is slow and they can hit monthly-hours limits.

The SnapFlood Play Store listing (com.snapflood) gives content the website lacks: developer 'RaftWaters', category Social, 100+ downloads, content rating Everyone, last updated Jul 26, 2026, support email raftwaters@gmail.com. It also credits funders the site never names: DST-SPLICE Climate Change Programme, National Network Programme on Urban Climate (NUC) under NMSKCC, and the Government of India AI CoE for Sustainable Cities. NOTE: the listing's 'About the developer' name reads 'Suresh Regonda' — a typo for Satish.

Teaching is 10 bare course titles with no course codes, no level (UG/PG), no semester, no year, no syllabus. Verbatim: Engineering Hydrology; Open Channel Hydraulics; Fundamentals of RS & GIS; RS & GIS Lab; Fluid Mechanics Lab; Engineering Hydrology and Hydrologic Systems; Applied Computational Laboratory; Hydraulic and Hydrologic Simulation Lab; Climate Monitoring and Variability; RS, GIS and Climate Change.
recommendations: Fix the domain reality first. Before any build decision, confirm satishregonda.in is actually registered and get nameservers pointed somewhere. Then decide what raftwaters.in should be — it is unregistered/undelegated, so 'link out to raftwaters.in' is currently a dead link. Safer plan for launch: host RAFT as /raft on satishregonda.in, and add the external link later only once raftwaters.in resolves.

Model 8 CMS collections, each backed by one Google Sheet tab so the professor edits rows not pages: publications, people, courses, projects, products, news/posts, press, and pages (free-text blocks). The existing content maps cleanly onto these — nothing in the current site needs a bespoke type.

Make `publications` a Sheet with columns: id, type (journal|chapter|conference|seminar), authors, year, title, venue, volume, pages, doi, url, note. Then derive the section headings (A–F) from `type` rather than hand-authoring them. This kills the current failure mode where a section header ('E. Invited Seminars') holds only 2 items and looks broken.

Make `people` ONE Sheet with columns: name, role (phd|mtech|ug|alumnus), status (current|graduated), topic, photo, start_year, end_year, viva_date, placement, blurb, co_supervisor. Render Students, Alumni and the RAFT team page from the SAME rows — that structurally prevents the current RAFT-vs-Students divergence, which is the single worst content bug on the site.

Add a `placement` column and fill it in. Every strong faculty site answers 'where did they go?'. Right now there are 6 PhD and 9 M.Tech alumni named with zero destination information — the highest-value new content on the whole site and the cheapest to collect.

Merge the Students page and the RAFT page's people section, but keep RAFT as its own rich page. RAFT's real distinguishing content is the mission paragraph, the 10 headshots, the per-person research blurbs (which the Students page lacks), SnapFlood, Sixer Tweet, VarshaMitra and UFIS. That is a genuinely good single-page story — it just needs the people pulled from the shared collection.

Build a proper Contact block from the IITH-verified data (Room B-212, Dept. of Civil Engineering, IIT Hyderabad, Kandi-502284, Sangareddy, Telangana; satishr@ce.iith.ac.in; +91 40 2359 6315) and use real mailto: links. Drop the '.at.' obfuscation — it does nothing against modern scrapers and reads as amateur. Resolve the 502284/502285 and 2301-6315/2359-6315 conflicts with him directly.

Add the identity/profile links that are entirely absent: Google Scholar (https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=cTXdUlUAAAAJ), ResearchGate, ORCID (he needs one if he lacks it), and a downloadable CV PDF. A faculty site with no CV link is the most conspicuous omission here.

Add a `news` collection and seed it with real, verified items so the blog does not launch empty: SnapFlood app update Jul 2026; 2026 papers in Urban Climate / WRR / JHRS; Guniganti PhD viva Feb 2026; Vaishnavi B viva Aug 2026; three 2026 M.Tech graduations; the Routledge chapter (2025); the 2023 UFIS press wave.
Add a `press` collection with the three verified articles (NewsMeter, The Hans India, Deccan Chronicle) and the UFIS YouTube video. This is free credibility the current site throws away.

Re-key Teaching into a `courses` Sheet with columns: code, title, level, semester, years_taught, description. Get the actual IITH course codes (CE-prefixed) from him — bare titles read as a placeholder list.

Do the image migration via Google Takeout, not scraping. All 22 sitesv/ URLs 403 to scripts. Budget for re-shooting or re-sourcing: there is no portrait of him, the two SnapFlood sample photos are third-party press images (Hindustan Times / The Hindu) that carry licensing risk if republished, and the Sixer guidelines exist only as a flat image that must be retyped as HTML.

Fix the publication data during migration rather than porting the errors: strip the trailing period from the JHM DOI, replace the dead Elsevier authors.elsevier.com link with the DOI, correct the Anupoju ASCE DOI, and split the two Brown et al. 2014 DOIs (.030 / .028). Add the missing DOIs for the pre-2011 papers, which currently have none.
Add Akansha Maity to the people sheet, and audit the rest against cc.iith.ac.in/students.html and the Civil dept listing — the personal site is not the authoritative roster it should be.

Pick one RAFT expansion and enforce it everywhere. The Play Store and SnapFlood page say 'Rainfall-runoff Analysis and Forecasting Tools'; the RAFT page says 'Rainfall-runoff Analysis modelling and Forecasting Tools'. Recommend the shorter Play Store form since it is already public-facing on an app listing.

Give the funded-projects list real structure (agency, collaborators, role, start/end, status) — currently it is four prose bullets with '[Completed]' tacked on the end, and it omits the funders named in the Play Store listing (DST-SPLICE, NUC/NMSKCC, AI CoE for Sustainable Cities).

Drop UA-138718262-1 and either install GA4 or, better for a minimal academic site, a lightweight privacy-friendly analytics script. Add per-page titles, meta descriptions, canonical tags and og:image — every page currently shares the title 'Satish R'.

### 2.12 ORPHAN — Climate Extremes, Societal Resiliency, Krishna River Basin

Title: **ClimateExtremes, Societal Resiliency and Krishna River Basin** [missing space]
Subtitle: Understanding Space-Time Variability of Climate Extremes for Societal Resiliency in Indonesia and India — **Workshop report** → https://drive.google.com/file/d/1CFDFK-2kgjD6mGr5MTK1_cmrsZ9IIhZx/view?usp=sharing (HTTP 200)

> Climate extremes, for example, floods, droughts and heatwave exhibit significant spatial- and temporal- variation in their magnitude and frequency. Also, its socio-economic consequences, which are mostly negative impacts, do vary with region. In this context, it is important to understand these climate extremes exclusively from science aspect, and importantly its linkages including impacts from socio-economic aspects. The enhanced understanding, broadly, enable better decision making, consequently increase the resiliency of a system. However, the fact that each region has unique climate and socio-economic signature makes the entire analysis from scientific understanding to drawing mitigation measures specific to the region. As part of the study, two regions two different countries, i.e., India (Krishna River Basin) and Indonesia (Serayu River Basin) are selected to understand similarities and differences of climate extremes across different space and time scales for societal resiliency.
>
> The proposal has two main objectives, i.e., 1. Scientific understanding of hydroclimate extremes; 2. Translation of scientific understanding into the decision making to increase the societal resiliency. The first objective is mostly straightforward and its difficulty depends on the complexity of the basin related physical mechanisms. The second objective is more than suggesting a scheme. The task involves identifying existing systems and understanding strategies for managing floods and droughts in urban, agriculture and water resources management contexts talking with different levels of various stakeholders. As part of it, Focus Group Discussion (FGD) and workshop with relevant stakeholders of the Krishna River Basin is planned at the IIT Hyderabad on 7th and 8th January, 2020.
